TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Fiordland approaches
DATE 19 January 2029 · 0520 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 95 min, closes at 142
Type 054A frigate. Photo: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Scott Ta... · Public domain · cropped

FIORDLAND APPROACHES, 0520. The group is in the Tasman. HULL 334, the diesel boat working the New Zealand side, needs her tender, and MV AUSTRAL COMPLIANCE, the AMS coaster, is to meet her this morning in the Milford cruise traffic west of Puysegur.

KIWI 05, a New Zealand Poseidon out of Invercargill, flies a racetrack over this approach every morning. Your screen is the loud one: take the decoy station on the cray grounds to the east, radiate every search set it has, and still be on station at the half hour. Only then does the tender's arrival count.

The tender and the boat go to the holding position quietly, some thirty miles west of the decoy station. If the aircraft puts a class on HULL 334, the rendezvous is known and the operation has failed. Answer nothing on the radio. Illuminate nothing: no fire-control radar goes near the aircraft.
A cruise ship bound for Milford, a Bluff cray boat and an Otago longliner are in the approach.
Fleet headquarters, southern tasking
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The boat off Fiordland has a week of patrol left in her and none of it is worth anything without her tender. The screen draws the patrol's eye and keeps it; the tender and the boat meet where the aircraft is not looking. Answer nothing on the radio. Illuminate nothing. Kiwi 05 is New Zealand's, and nothing the group does this morning gives Wellington a reason to say otherwise.
• Hold the decoy station at the half hour, then bring the tender and Hull 334 to the holding position
• Keep Hull 334 off their plot: do not let the patrol classify her
• Answer nothing: fire on nothing
• Bring the screen off the decoy station intact
• Harm no cruise ship or fishing boat

Your screen with its flight, holding the decoy station. Allocated: MV Austral Compliance, the AMS tender, and Hull 334, a Type 039C, dived. Watching: Kiwi 05, an RNZAF P-8A out of Invercargill. Neutral: a cruise ship, a cray boat and a longliner.

The planned window is 95 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 47 minutes more; the operation is closed at 142 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
